intended_object: The profinite completion Ẑ of the infinite cyclic group ℤ, viewed as a profinite group written multiplicatively. This comes from the docstring and from its use as the source of the canonical map Ẑ → G that sends 1 to g.
explanation: The definition applies Mathlib's general profinite completion `ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.completion` to `Multiplicative ℤ`, which is ℤ written as a multiplicative group. That completion is the limit of G/N over the finite-index normal subgroups N. The group is lifted with `ULift` so that it can live in any universe. The result is exactly the standard Ẑ = lim ℤ/nℤ, with its group structure and topology. It is the profinite completion of one specific group, so it is not too narrow: Mathlib's general construction is used directly rather than rewritten by hand. I found no dedicated Ẑ in Mathlib (searches for `ZHat`, `zHat` and `ProfiniteInt` returned nothing), so there is no other counterpart to cite.
